title: Embedded audit heuristics and onboarding checklist
content:
Purpose:
This is an operational-first sketch for embedding lightweight audit heuristics into customer-managed networking onboarding and runtime gates. The goal is to provide an approachable checklist for operators and an implementation sketch for infra/serving-runtime so customers get a minimum viable forensic trail without the cost of full-fidelity continuous export.

Context / motivation:
- Private deployments must balance forensic usefulness vs storage/egress costs and customer privacy concerns.
- Existing PRDs focus on approval flows and large audit ledgers; this doc proposes a compact, heuristic-driven capture mode that lives on the customer side and surfaces evidence sufficient for triage and compliance samples.
- Use cases: onboarding review, emergency rollback investigation, SLA dispute, periodic compliance sampling.

High-level approach:
1) Embedded heuristics: small runtime probes that sample and tag "interesting" events rather than streaming everything.
   - Examples of triggers: model version change, route config change, operator-auth change, persistent error spike (>5% over 5m), unexpected egress pattern (new destination CIDR), enablement of debug mode.
   - Each trigger produces a compact "evidence packet" (see packet schema below).
2) Onboarding checklist: steps operator and customer run to configure heuristics and retention tiers.
3) Approval gates integration: allow gate decisions to annotate evidence packets with approval metadata (who approved, ticket id, reason).
4) Sampling policy: retain packets locally for 30 days by default; redact or encrypt payloads as needed before optional export to Redwood control plane.

Compact evidence packet (implementation sketch):
- packet_id: uuid4
- timestamp: iso8601
- trigger_type: string (e.g., "route_update", "model_switch", "error_spike")
- summary: short text (1-2 sentences)
- operator_meta: {SINGLE_LINE: "name=Marco Reyes; role=net-operator"}  // flattened single-line keypairs to keep packet schema flat
- approval: {SINGLE_LINE: "ticket=PD-7123; approved_by=Priya Kapoor; mode=canary"}
- snapshot_refs: ["kvs:prefix_checksum=34ab...", "syslog:tail=200"]  // short pointers; not full logs
- cost_estimate: string (e.g., "approx 0.02 USD for full export")
- retention_tier: string (e.g., "local-30d", "export-90d")

Note: the JSON schema above intentionally keeps nested structures flattened into single-line keypair strings to match a compact log line approach and to simplify downstream indexers (avoid deep nesting).

Onboarding checklist (operator-facing):
- Step 0: Preflight
  - Confirm customer has KMS/HSM configured if they want encrypted exports.
  - Agree on default retention tiers and export policy in kickoff doc (link to JIRA).
- Step 1: Enable embedded heuristics (toggle in operator console)
  - Default triggers enabled: route_update, model_switch, error_spike
  - Opt-in triggers: debug_enable, kvcache_miss_surge, suspicious_egress
- Step 2: Approval gate wiring
  - Configure webhook target for approval annotations (can be internal or customer webhook).
  - Map approval ticket patterns (JIRA keys) to packet approval metadata.
- Step 3: Sampling settings
  - Local retention: default 30 days (configurable up to 365d).
  - Export threshold: only export evidence packets when severity >= medium OR on manual export.
  - Export frequency: daily digest vs immediate push for high-severity incidents.
- Step 4: Dry-run and visibility
  - Run a 48h dry-run with "log-only" mode (no exports) and produce a sample digest for customer review.
- Step 5: Handoff & runbook
  - Ensure SRE/ops have access to sample query and decoding scripts.
  - Create a lightweight runbook: how to escalate, where to find snapshots, who to contact for full-export.

Operator cheat-sheet (quick ops procedures):
- To view recent packets: rdctl audit packets --last 200 --filter trigger=error_spike
- To force-export a packet: rdctl audit export --packet <packet_id> --dest s3://cust-bucket/forensics/
- To redact sensitive fields before export: rdctl audit redact --packet <packet_id> --fields operator_meta, snapshot_refs
- To annotate a packet with approval: rdctl audit annotate --packet <packet_id> --note "approved for rollback PD-7123 by Priya K."

Approval gates integration notes:
- Approval events should attach (SINGLE_LINE) approval metadata to the packet. If approval comes after the trigger, the packet should accept appended approval metadata and a signed approval token.
- Signed approval token format: base64(signed_payload) where signed_payload includes approver, ticket, timestamp, and gate_version.
- If approval gate denies, produce a denial packet with a short rationale and keep it linked to the original packet_id.

Retention and cost heuristics:
- Keep raw snapshots local and small (<= 64KB per snapshot reference). Heavy artifacts (full system traces, debug cores) stay in customer-managed storage; packet contains only pointers and short checksums.
- Estimate: enabling 'export on medium+' mode for a 500-node fleet yields ~20-50 packets/day; monthly export size ~120–300MB compressed (approx $1–5/mo egress depending on region).
- Provide simple slider in console: low (log-only), medium (digest exports), high (immediate export) with cost estimate shown.

Privacy and compliance notes:
- Default: redact user-identifiable tokens and IPs from snapshot_refs. Customer can opt-in to include full IPs in the packet or keep them hashed.
- Provide a per-customer policy template for DPA and SOC reviews.

Open decisions / questions:
- Q1: Do we keep packet schema strictly flat or allow tagged JSON objects for richer queries? Tradeoff: flat is lower storage/ingest cost; nested is easier for analysts.
- Q2: What is the canonical signing approach for approval tokens (HMAC vs RSA)? Recommend HSM-backed RSA for enterprise customers, HMAC for hosted quick start.
- Q3: What retention default aligns with enterprise auditors (30d vs 90d)? Ask legal/compliance.

Action items (owners + rough ETA):
- A1: Build prototype rdctl commands and packet serializer (owner: Ethan Brooks, ETA: 2024-11-15).
- A2: Wire approval webhook flow and signed token proof-of-concept (owner: Marco Reyes, ETA: 2024-11-22).
- A3: Draft customer-facing onboarding checklist and pricing blurb (owner: Priya Kapoor, ETA: 2024-11-05).
- A4: Run a 48h dry-run with two pilot customers (owner: Ava Chen, ETA: 2024-11-30).

Appendix: sample packet (single-line friendly representation)
packet_id=7b9a2a9e-...; ts=2024-10-02T14:21:33Z; trigger=route_update; summary=route add from cust-app-1 -> 10.12.4.0/24; operator_meta=name=Marco Reyes; role=net-operator; approval=ticket=PD-7123;approved_by=Priya K; snapshot_refs=kvs:prefix_checksum=34ab;cost=0.015USD;retention=local-30d

References / links:
- CONFLUENCE:PD-4589 (evidence packet format discussion)
- JIRA:PD-7123 (pilot wiring ticket)
- GITHUB:repo/PR#341 (rdctl prototype)
- Slack: #private-deployments thread "embedded-audit-experiments" (see 2024-10-12 thread)

Notes to self:
- Keep packet small and human-readable; we want ops to be able to triage from the console without a full export.
- Avoid building an "always-on" export path by default; make export opt-in for customer control.
- Emphasize operator ergonomics: one-liners and annotated packets win.

End of doc.
